odd_element_definitions.description: Measure from ( Source ): The centerline of one lane marking (such as a dashed or solid line that separates lanes), To the centerline of the adjacent lane marking . Assumption : The current analysis shows that only two nominal miles of the MVP route (Round Trip) account for less than 11 ft of lane width. Initial Q3_Layer1_ODD.pdf

The K value represents the reciprocal of the radius of curvature. Mathematically, it's calculated as: K=1/R​ Where: K = Curvature factor (in 1/meter) R = Radius of curvature (in meter) Counter clockwise is denoted in - (negative). Clockwise is denoted in + (positive) Note: This curvature range doesn't apply for intersections or sharp surface street turns.

odd_element_definitions.description: Steady wind on the Beaufort scale (Calm..Gale), matching the Jama Wind > Steady wind sub-elements. Derived from Open-Meteo 10 m wind speed (knots); breakdowns by month.
Rain intensity classes (WMO: None/Light<2.5/Moderate<7.6/Heavy mm/hr) from Open-Meteo hourly precipitation; breakdowns by month.

Sun Angle (ambient lighting by apparent solar altitude): High >20 deg, Low 0-20 deg, Twilight 0..-6 deg, Night <-6 deg. This characterization measures Direct Sun (glare): Low sun angle (0-20 deg) AND vehicle heading within +/-30 deg of the sun azimuth, computed from local solar position (NOAA) vs route segment headings over 2021-01-01..2025-12-31 (America/Chicago, incl. DST). The Direct-Sun measurement conceptually maps to the Jama sub-element 'Sun glare Angle' (TORC-ODD-39), currently Out of Scope; note Jama defines glare as <=12 deg while the data-team uses <=20 deg. Distribution metric = glare mile-hours/day by route heading sector. Each route is characterized in its own single travel direction (the core southbound legs); the northbound return legs are separate routes (crawl_i_35_*_return) and are not covered by this report.
odd_element_definitions.odd_path: L5 Environmental Condition > Lighting Conditions > Sun Angle
